headline:
A well-kept space.
A better working day.
intro: Cleaning programs shaped around your building, your people, and the way your business works.
serviceTitle: A plan for the way your building works.
serviceIntro: Each facility has its own traffic, materials, and quiet hours. Start with the spaces that matter to your team.

offers.title: Offices & workplaces
offers.text: Support a welcoming arrival and an orderly end to the day.

offers.title: Retail & studios
offers.text: Keep customer-facing spaces ready for their next visitor.

offers.title: Shared buildings
offers.text: Bring a defined scope to the areas everyone uses.

story.title: A checklist is only useful when it fits.
story.text: We begin with a walkthrough: the footprint, floor finishes, traffic patterns, and tasks your team needs handled. The resulting plan makes responsibilities visible.
points: A schedule matched to building use

guide.title: Clarity at every handoff.
guide.intro: Good facility care depends on more than a list of tasks. Everyone should know what is included, when work happens, and how to raise an issue.

notes.title: Walk the space
notes.text: Review rooms, floor types, high-traffic areas, storage, waste handling, and any restrictions. Sensitive or specialized environments need their own qualified scope.

notes.title: Agree the schedule
notes.text: Choose service windows around occupancy, deliveries, meetings, and opening hours. Separate recurring tasks from periodic deep work.

notes.title: Make the scope visible
notes.text: Document task frequency, responsibility, consumable arrangements, and areas excluded from routine service. Avoid vague “everything included” promises.

notes.title: Review what changes
notes.text: A new team, layout, or busy season changes a building. Schedule a way to update the checklist and report issues without interrupting daily work.

faq.q: Can the schedule fit around our team?
faq.a: The sample planner includes early morning, evening, and weekend windows. A real walkthrough would confirm access rules, security, occupancy, and staffing.
That belongs in the agreed scope. Cleaning products, restroom consumables, and waste services may have different arrangements and should be listed separately.

faq.q: Do you cover clinical or industrial cleaning?
faq.a: Those environments may require specialist protocols. This example covers ordinary commercial spaces and does not claim medical or hazardous-material cleaning capabilities.
